title: How Council 2 reached its verdict
question: Should I personally take part in the French protests of autumn 2026?
process: Working groups: three groups (events & policing, movements & calendar, law & risk), each a researcher then an adversarial verifier.
Seven seats, including two new ones (Abstainer, Local Realist), wrote independent opening positions.
Three rounds of two rooms, 4 of 7 seats drawn at random per room; each room reported agreements, disagreements, information requests and a reframe flag.
Fact desk between rounds (five passes); reframe loop available, not used.
Chairman draft → internal quality audit (same process) → revision; v3 after an external review.

stats.label: external review of the final report

stages.subtitle: a researcher, then an adversarial verifier

cards.title: WG1 · Events & policing
cards.text: Violence started around midday at assembly points. A second death was reported (cause unknown). A parliamentary inquiry was voted.

cards.title: WG2 · Movements & calendar
cards.text: Four distinct strands. The '12 Nov' date is unsupported. The Bordeaux '5 Nov' link shows the 13 Oct route.

cards.title: WG3 · Law & risk
cards.text: EU and non-EU residents face different rules. Kettling is still lawful. An arrest leaves a TAJ police-file entry.

cards.text: Leverage differs by strand. 5 Nov stays relevant under every budget scenario.

cards.title: Room B · Red team
cards.text: Settled 2 of the 3 contested cells. Listed every remaining breach of the quality rules.

Joining a banned one: a €135 fine

loop.text: Any room could raise a reframe flag and send the council back to triage. All six rooms judged that the facts refined the question rather than overturning it.

final.title: Chairman → audit → revision

cards.title: Chairman's draft
cards.text: 12 sections, written by a separate agent with no seat on the council.

cards.title: Internal quality audit
cards.text: 11 required fixes, among them one line that took a side, the fine amounts, the face-covering offence, unused glossary terms.

final.verdict: The answer depends on your demand and your risk profile. Staying home is legitimate. If you go, choose a declared daytime march, walk in the main body and leave early.
